topic: decode shape now faster than vendor; prefill still short; cube path blocked

blocked_paths.cube_gemm: T.gemm device codegen fails on this CANN: undefined asc_set_gm2l1_nz_para / asc_set_l0c_copy_nz_para / asc_unit_flag_mode / asc_quant_mode / asc_relu_pre_mode. The official example_gemm.py fails identically, so this is a toolchain incompatibility, not our usage.
blocked_paths.bf16_fma: vmula with bf16 operands and an f32 accumulator is rejected; there is no mixed-precision multiply-accumulate.
blocked_paths.vld_conversion: vld never converts; vcvt is mandatory, so the two-pass design cannot drop a conversion.

decode_64x4096.note: kernel is ~29% faster than vendor in this window

ceiling_reasoning: the kernel is vector-bound; vector busy was ~89.6 us at 122.6 us total, so this two-pass vector algorithm has a structural ceiling near 0.8x for prefill even with perfect overlap. Removing cube and bf16-fma as options leaves no known way to cut the per-element vector op count by the ~25% needed.
status: decode above 1.0 in a single-process paired measurement; prefill still ~0.62x; neither is witness-audited and no acceptance has run
not_proven: no witness audit, no multi-process confirmation, no independent acceptance; prefill parity not achieved
review_correction: The historical interpretation claiming a proven bottleneck, performance ceiling, compiler-wide limitation, or cross-run speedup is retracted. The measurements were exploratory and insufficiently paired; profiler utilization is not a proof of a hard bound. The archived candidate initially used an invalid dtype spelling and must be verified separately. Preserve numerical observations as historical only.
